title: Adoption agency algorithm issues (sanitizer and intended parent)
body:
While reviewing #12758 (`stream*HTML*`), we identified several pre-existing issues in the HTML parser's [adoption agency algorithm](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#adoption-agency-algorithm) (particularly its interaction with parser-level sanitization and custom element registries, as well as `intendedParent` resolution).

Filing these separately so they can be addressed independently of #12758:

1. **`furthestBlock` retains a null custom element registry when reparented out of a removed `formattingElement`**:
   When an element is created inside an ancestor whose sanitizer action is `"Remove"`, [create an element for a token](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#create-an-element-for-the-token) sets its `custom element registry` to null. If the adoption agency algorithm later reparents `furthestBlock` (via `lastNode`) into `commonAncestor` because `formattingElement` was removed, `furthestBlock`'s `custom element registry` remains null even though it is now in the kept subtree, preventing subsequent descendant elements from looking up a registry via their intended parent.

2. **`furthestBlock`'s children briefly enter the target tree when `formattingElement` is `"Remove"`**:
   Step 4.14 inserts `lastNode` (`furthestBlock`, along with its existing children) at the appropriate place for inserting a node given `commonAncestor` before steps 4.15–4.16 create `newElement` (which is not inserted when `formattingElement`'s sanitizer action is `"Remove"`) and move `furthestBlock`'s children into `newElement`. As a result, when `commonAncestor` is in the live tree, `furthestBlock`'s children are momentarily inserted into the target tree (triggering insertion steps, `connectedCallback`, `iframe` loading, or `script` preparation) even though they end up inside the removed `newElement`.

3. **Clones created in the inner loop below a removed ancestor get the live document and custom element registry**:
   In the inner loop (step 4.13.6), [create an element for a token](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#create-an-element-for-the-token) is always called with `commonAncestor` as `intendedParent`. If an outer cloned formatting element in the inner loop (or `formattingElement` itself) has a sanitizer action of `"Remove"`, inner clones whose own sanitizer action is `"Keep"` still receive `commonAncestor`'s document and custom element registry (allowing synchronous custom element constructors to run in the live document), even though they end up appended to a removed ancestor subtree.

4. **Inner loop passes `commonAncestor` directly as `intendedParent`**:
   Step 4.13.6 passes `commonAncestor` directly as `intendedParent` to [create an element for a token](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#create-an-element-for-the-token), rather than the `target parent` of the [appropriate place for inserting a node](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#appropriate-place-for-inserting-a-node) given `commonAncestor`. When `commonAncestor` is a `<template>` element or triggers foster parenting, the intended parent used during cloning diverges from normal parser insertion (`insert a foreign element`), affecting `nodeDocument` and `custom element registry` lookup.
